Working notes — ticket routing

Observed 10 tickets (REQ-2400–2409). Options seen: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Key result:
- Only successful routing: REQ-2405 → C accepted. Context: large shipment, north region, from Client Services, comment explicitly said “came in through the regional office.”
- All other tried C options were rejected (REQ-2400, 2401, 2403, 2404, 2406, 2407, 2408, 2409).
- B was tried once and rejected: REQ-2402, large refund, south region, Client Services, “client asking twice.”

Useful rule:
- Do not select C just because the ticket mentions region, size, sender, or urgency. Select C only when there is an explicit regional-office routing cue, e.g. “came in through the regional office.”
- B priority desk is not supported by evidence yet; the one B attempt was rejected.
- Boilerplate phrases (“client asking twice,” “second attempt,” “same as last month,” “scanned not typed”) did not make C or B valid.
- Likely default for no explicit cue is A standard queue, but A has not yet been tested. Prefer A when no strong cue for B/C.
- Track request type, region, size, sender, and exact comments. The explicit routing phrase appears more important than type/region/size.

Caution: small sample. If an option is rejected, avoid repeating same choice for similar tickets unless a new explicit cue appears.

Working notes — ticket routing

Observed 20 tickets (REQ-2400–2419). Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Evidence:
- Only known accepted routing: REQ-2405 → C. Details: shipment request, large, north, Client Services, comment “came in through the regional office.”
- A has now been tried and rejected 8 times: REQ-2410, 2411, 2412, 2414, 2416, 2417, 2418, 2419. Varied request types, regions, sizes, senders, and boilerplate. A is not a safe default.
- C rejected 10 times, including REQ-2413 and 2415 despite explicit “came in through the regional office.” So that phrase is not sufficient by itself. The new C failures were refunds; the only C success was a shipment.
- B tried once and rejected: REQ-2402, large refund, south, Client Services, “client asking twice.” Still unsupported.
- Boilerplate (“same as last month,” “second attempt,” “asking twice,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt”) does not determine routing.

Working hypotheses:
- C may be valid only for shipment requests with an explicit regional-office cue; current success fits, but sample is tiny.
- Refund requests with regional-office phrase are not C (REQ-2413, 2415).
- A is disproven as default; avoid repeating rejected choices for similar tickets unless a new cue appears.
- Track exact request type and explicit routing phrase; these look more predictive than region/size/sender/urgency.

Caution: 1 success out of 20. Do not overgeneralize. For a similar shipment with regional-office cue, C is best-supported; otherwise no option is well-supported.

Working notes — ticket routing

Observed 29 tickets (REQ-2400–2429). Options A, B, C; D is now observed.

Accepted routings:
- C: REQ-2405 only — shipment, large, north, Client Services, “came in through the regional office.”
- D: REQ-2420, 2424, 2427 — all invoice requests. 2420/2424: south, large/small, Regional Ops/Field Sales, “No rush, but please confirm receipt.” 2427: east, small, Regional Ops, “client asking twice.”

Rejected:
- A: 8 rejections (REQ-2410–2412, 2414, 2416–2419). Not a safe default.
- B: 1 rejection (REQ-2402, large refund).
- C: 10 rejections, including refunds with explicit regional-office cue (2413, 2415). Only C success was a shipment.
- D: rejected for all tried refunds/claims (2421–2423, 2425, 2429) and north invoices (2426, 2428).

Working hypotheses:
- D is best-supported for invoice requests, especially south/east; north invoices with D failed. Sample small.
- C may be valid only for shipment requests with an explicit regional-office cue.
- Refund/claim requests currently have no well-supported option; D, A, B, C have all failed or are unsupported. Avoid D for refunds/claims unless new cue appears.
- Boilerplate (“no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “asking twice,” “same as last month,” “second attempt,” scanned-not-typed) does not determine routing by itself.
- Track request type + region for D. Region may matter more than sender/urgency.

Caution: only 4 accepted routings out of 29. Do not overgeneralize.

Working notes — ticket routing

Observed 39 tickets in REQ-2400–2439. Options A–D.

Accepted routings:
- C: REQ-2405 only — shipment, large, north, Client Services, “came in through the regional office.”
- D: REQ-2420, 2424, 2427, 2435, 2439 — all invoices. South/east. 2435 east/large/Finance; 2439 south/small/Regional Ops.
- B: REQ-2432, 2434 — claims, east. 2432 small/Finance Desk; 2434 large/Client Services, “regional office” cue.

Rejected:
- A: many, including 2410–2412, 2414, 2416–2419, 2430 (east claim). Not a safe default.
- B: 2402 large refund; 2431 south large shipment; 2438 north small refund.
- C: many, including refunds with regional cue (2413, 2415), 2437 south shipment. Only success was north shipment with regional cue.
- D: refunds/claims 2421–2423, 2425, 2429; north invoices 2426, 2428; refunds 2433 south, 2436 north. Avoid D for refunds/claims.

Working hypotheses:
- D is best-supported for invoice requests, especially south/east. North invoices with D failed. Sample small.
- B may be valid for east claims (small/large), regardless sender/boilerplate. Not for shipments/refunds.
- C may be valid only for shipment requests with explicit regional-office cue; not south shipment without cue.
- Refund requests: no well-supported option; A/B/C/D have failed or are unsupported. Avoid B/D for refunds unless new cue appears.
- Boilerplate (“no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “asking twice,” “same as last month,” scanned-not-typed) does not determine routing alone.
- Track request type + region + sender; region/type matter more than urgency.

Caution: only 8 accepted routings out of 39. Do not overgeneralize.

Working notes — ticket routing

Observed 49 tickets REQ-2400–2449. Options A–D.

Accepted:
- D: REQ-2420, 2424, 2427, 2435, 2439, 2441, 2444. All invoices; mostly south/east. 2441 south small invoice with regional-office cue; 2444 south small invoice. Best for invoices.
- B: REQ-2432, 2434, 2443, 2448. Claims, east, small/large; sender/boilerplate irrelevant. Not for refunds/shipments.
- C: REQ-2405 only — north large shipment with explicit regional-office cue. Not invoices: 2447 north large invoice with same cue failed.
- A: REQ-2440 north small invoice; REQ-2445 north small refund; REQ-2446 east small refund. Emerging for some invoices/refunds, but not safe default.

Rejected:
- A: many, including 2410–2412, 2414, 2416–2419, 2430 east claim, 2442 south small shipment.
- B: 2402 large refund; 2431 south large shipment; 2438 north small refund; 2449 south small refund.
- C: many, including refunds with regional cue 2413, 2415; 2437 south shipment; 2447 north invoice.
- D: refunds/claims 2421–2423, 2425, 2429; north invoices 2426, 2428; refunds 2433 south, 2436 north.

Hypotheses:
- D best for invoices, especially south/east. North invoices failed with D/C; A accepted one north small invoice.
- B valid for east claims regardless size/sender/boilerplate. Not for shipments/refunds.
- C valid only for shipment with regional-office cue; not south shipment without cue.
- Refunds: avoid B/D. A accepted small north/east refunds (2445, 2446); still thin.
- Boilerplate does not determine routing alone.
- Track type + region + size + sender; type/region strongest.

Caution: only 15 accepted of 49. Do not overgeneralize.

Working notes — ticket routing (REQ-2400–2459; options A–D)

Accepted:
D: invoices, esp. south/east. 2420, 2424, 2427, 2435, 2439, 2441, 2444, 2457 (east large). Best for invoices.
B: east claims, any size/sender/boilerplate. 2432, 2434, 2443, 2448, 2451. Not refunds/shipments.
C: north shipments (large): 2405, 2452, 2453, 2459. Also north small transfer w/ regional cue: 2455. Not east transfers (2450, 2454 rejected); not invoices/refunds.
A: small refunds north/east/south: 2445, 2446, 2456, 2458. Also 2440 north small invoice. Best current option for small refunds.

Rejected/limits:
A: many, incl. 2410–2412, 2414, 2416–2419, 2430, 2442.
B: 2402, 2431, 2438, 2449.
C: 2413, 2415, 2437, 2447; 2450 east small transfer, 2454 east large transfer.
D: refunds/claims 2421–2423, 2425, 2429; north invoices 2426, 2428; refunds 2433, 2436.

Hypotheses:
- D for invoices; north invoices failed, A took one.
- B for east claims; size/sender/boilerplate irrelevant.
- C for north shipments/transfers, not east transfers, not invoices/refunds. Regional cue not sufficient for C.
- Refunds: use A if small; avoid B/D. Large refund unknown.
- Type and region strongest; size next; sender/boilerplate not decisive.

Caution: 23 accepted of 59. Do not overgeneralize.

Working notes — ticket routing (REQ-2400–2469; options A–D)

Accepted:
D: invoices, esp. south/east, likely larger. 2420, 2424, 2427, 2435, 2439, 2441, 2444, 2457.
B: east claims, but now likely smaller only. 2432, 2434, 2443, 2448, 2451. Not refunds/shipments.
C: north shipments (large): 2405, 2452, 2453, 2459, 2468. Also north small transfer w/ regional cue: 2455. Not east transfers 2450, 2454; not invoices/refunds.
A: small refunds north/east/south: 2445, 2446, 2456, 2458. Also north small invoice 2440; north small renewal 2464. Best for small refunds.

New rejects/limits:
A: large south refund 2460 rejected; east small renewal 2466 rejected; many prior.
B: east large claims 2461, 2465 rejected; north large claim 2462 rejected. So B not all east claims; not north claims.
C: 2413, 2415, 2437, 2447; east small transfer 2450, east large transfer 2454.
D: small south invoice 2463 rejected; east large shipment 2467; south small renewal 2469; prior refunds/claims and north invoices 2426, 2428.

Hypotheses:
- D for invoices, but fails small south invoice; maybe large/regional subset.
- B for east claims, but large east claims fail; B not north claims.
- C for north shipments/transfers; north large shipment confirmed. Not east transfers.
- A for small refunds and north small renewal; not large refunds, not east small renewal.
- Renewals unclear: A north small accepted; A east small rejected; D south small rejected.
- Claims: B east small likely; large east and north fail.
- Type/region strongest; size matters for claims/refunds/invoices; sender/boilerplate not decisive.

Caution: 25 accepted of 69. Do not overgeneralize.

Working notes — ticket routing (REQ-2400–2479; options A–D)

Accepted patterns:
A: small refunds N/E/S; N small invoice/renewal; E small audit 2471; E large cancellation 2478. Rejected S small onboarding 2470. Best for small refunds/audits, some cancellations; not onboarding.
B: E small claims likely (2432, 2434, 2443, 2448, 2451). Rejected E small onboarding 2477; E large claims 2461, 2465; N large claim 2462. Not refunds/shipments/onboarding.
C: N large shipments (2405, 2452, 2453, 2459, 2468); N small transfer 2455. Rejected E transfers 2450, 2454; N large audit 2474. Not invoices/refunds/audits.
D: invoices esp. S/E larger (2420, 2424, 2427, 2435, 2439, 2441, 2444, 2457); S large onboarding 2473; E large audit 2479. Rejected S small invoice 2463; S large audit 2472; E large onboarding 2475, 2476; E large shipment 2467; S small renewal 2469; N invoices 2426, 2428.

Unclear:
Renewals: A N small accepted; A E small rejected; D S small rejected.
Claims: B E small likely; large E/N fail.
Audits: A E small and D E large accepted; C N large and D S large rejected.
Onboarding: D S large accepted; A S small, B E small, D E large rejected.

Type/region strongest; size matters for claims/refunds/invoices/onboarding/audits. Sender/boilerplate not decisive.

Caution: 29 accepted of 79. Do not overgeneralize.
